title: Value of a Box OAuth access token in a token response or Bearer header
summary: A synthetic value of the access_token member of a pretty-printed token response, and after Authorization: Bearer in a raw request and a quoted curl -H argument.
rationale: The carrier is documented: the Box token endpoint response carries the access token in its access_token member, and the reference states the token is passed in an authorization header as Authorization: Bearer <Token>. Box states no prefix, alphabet or length, so the value is flagged because of where it sits, not because of its shape. The extent is the value only: the member name, the colon, the scheme word and the quotes are outside it. The expires_in number and the token_type word are not values of this credential.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the string value of the access_token member of a token response, or the value after Authorization: Bearer, is treated as a credential whatever its shape. Box documents the access_token response member and the Authorization: Bearer header (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and a generic attribution are the project's decisions. No subtype is inferred, and no prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

sources.supports: Returns a new Access Token that can be used to make authenticated API calls by passing along the token in a authorization header as follows Authorization: Bearer <Token>

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
